subject: Dedicated deployment footprint options — Nebularis
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@nebularis.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — initial ask

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our product team has sketched a roadmap where inference demand grows from ~100k gen tokens/day today to a steady-state 2.5M tokens/day over 9 months, with periodic spikes up to ~6M tokens/day during experiments. We need recommendations that meet two constraints: predictable unit economics for budgeting, and a minimum guaranteed capacity for SLA-sensitive routines (model scoring for diagnostics).

Specifically can you provide:
- 2–3 commitment profiles (cluster sizes and minimum GPUs) that balance cost vs latency reliability;
- a suggested ramp schedule (how to phase activation over 3, 6, 9 months);
- options for warm-start credits or soft burst allowance during experimental windows;
- any quick notes on fallback to hosted tiers in case of sustained overage.

Also attaching a short CSV with our expected daily token profile and 95p95 latency objective. Happy to jump on a call — Sam (cc) is our infra lead if you want deeper technical metrics.

Best,
Elena
VP Product, Nebularis Therapeutics

Attachments: nebularis_token_profile.csv (referenced)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@nebularis.ai>
Cc: Sam Vega <sam.vega@nebularis.ai>
Date: 2026-11-26T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial ask

Elena — thanks for the data and context. I pulled together three practical reservation options and an activation playbook; summary below and attached a formal PDF and onramp workbook. High level: we recommend starting with a conservative baseline that meets your SLA for critical scoring paths while enabling staged capacity to keep unit cost under control.

Option A — Conservative baseline (low CAPEX risk):
- Cluster: 8-GPU dedicated pool (A100-80GB equiv.)
- Minimum commit: 8 GPUs
- Expected steady throughput: ~1.2M tokens/day with 95p token latency ~85ms (with prefix cache)
- Ramp: activate month 0: 40% of baseline capacity; month 3: 70%; month 6: 100%
- Warm-start credits: 200K tokens/month included for spikes

Option B — Balanced (recommended for staged experiments):
- Cluster: 16-GPU pool
- Minimum commit: 12 GPUs (softly metered)
- Expected steady throughput: ~2.5M tokens/day with 95p latency ~65ms
- Ramp: month 0: 30% (pilot), month 2: 60%, month 5: 100%
- Burst allowance: up to 30% sustained burst for 72 hours; additional consumption billed at a predictable rate

Option C — Throughput-first (aggressive):
- Cluster: 32-GPU pool
- Minimum commit: 24 GPUs
- Expected steady throughput: ~5–6M tokens/day, 95p latency ~50–60ms
- Ramp: month 0: 20% pilot, month 1: 50%, month 3: 100%
- Warm-start: larger buffer + priority preemptible lanes for experiments

Common notes:
- All options include automatic prefix/KV caching and model-variant fallbacks to a slightly quantized profile to preserve SLOs under heavy load.
- Canary policy: we recommend a 7-day canary at each activation step to catch regressions; rollback triggers available.
- Costs: workbook lays out committed vs burst pricing and projected monthly token unit cost under each profile.

Next steps: if you prefer Option B we can send a tailored SOW and pricing sheet; Karhtik (cc) can add technical notes about prewarming windows and recommended quantization profiles.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Nebularis_Dedicated_Offer_v1.pdf; capacity-onramp-workbook.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@nebularis.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial ask (technical addendum)

Elena, Sam — quick technical addendum to Neha's commercial options. I wanted to call out three operational specifics that affect the minimum GPU floor and ramp timing: 

1) Model family and sequence length distribution: for longer sequences (2k+ tokens) effective throughput per GPU drops ~18–25%. If your diagnostics jobs have longer context we should bias toward the higher GPU counts in Option B/C or pre-split those workloads across a dedicated lane.

2) Warm-start and KV-cache population: we recommend a 48–72 hour prewarm for each major activation step for any route that needs steady 95p latency; that can be automated and covered by warm-start credits in the offer.

3) Quantization fallback: to keep UI-facing latency tight while lowering cost during non-critical windows, use a 4-bit quantized variant for non-SLA routes. We can provide per-route kernel profiles and expected latency delta (+10–20ms).

Operational implication: if Nebularis wants a hard minimum SLA-backed floor for scoring, lean toward "Minimum commit" values stated in the balanced/aggressive options rather than the pilot percentages. For a smoother ramp we can add a one-time warm-start credit top-up during month 1.

I'll sync with Marissa on onboarding cadence and with Neha on SOW language for the one-time warmup.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morris <elena@nebularis.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sam Vega <sam.vega@nebularis.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T16:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial ask

Team — thanks, this is very helpful. We like the flexibility in Option B and appreciate the prewarm guidance. A few quick decisions from our side:

- Preferred: Option B with Minimum commit = 12 GPUs; start pilot at 30% (as you suggested).
- Approve the 72-hour prewarm before the month-2 lift (please include the extra warm-start credit in the SOW).
- We will take the burst allowance for experiments but want a 30-day notice threshold before we exceed sustained burst more than 3x.

Next steps for Redwood: please send a statement of work and a draft purchase order with the 12-GPU minimum and the warm-start top-up. I'll loop Legal and Procurement and get a PO within 10 business days if the SOW matches. Marissa, can you also add onboarding milestones for model onboarding + two-week performance bake window?

I'll forward this thread internally to our procurement lead for sign-off.

Best,
Elena
VP Product, Nebularis Therapeutics
